title: Ireland planted ornamental rhododendrons in the 1700s to beautify country estates, but more than 200 years later, scientists say they are smothering ancient oak forests and preventing native trees from regenerating
description: Eighteenth-century landowners introduced ornamental rhododendrons for garden beauty. This invasive species later spread aggressively across Irish natural habitats. The plant creates dense shade, suppressing native vegetation and woodland regeneration. Conservationists now face a difficult and expensive task removing the shrub. Restoration efforts highlight the ecological risks of introducing non-native species.

title: Scientists Discover One-in-a-Million Soft-Tissue Fossil From a 450-Million-Year-Old Sea Creature
description: Scientists uncovered an ultra‐rare 450‐million‐year‐old crinoid soft‐tissue fossil, revealing how ancient sea creatures fed and lived in Earth’s earliest reef ecosystems.

title: Ancient bees used 20,000-year-old tooth sockets as nurseries in a Caribbean cave, and CT scans reveal the first known bee nests inside animal bones
description: Ancient animal skulls unearthed in a Caribbean cave have revealed a surprising chapter in bee history. For the first time, researchers have found fossilized bee nests dating back 20,000 years, ingeniously crafted within the empty tooth cavities of these ancient creatures. This discovery showcases the remarkable adaptability of solitary bees, who utilized these protected spaces to raise their young, offering a rare glimpse into prehistoric insect behavior.

title: Scientists Finally Found a 150-Million-Year Fossil That Captures the Exact Moment When Birds Lost Their Dinosaur Tails
description: For decades, scientists have searched for a fossil that could help explain one of evolution's biggest mysteries. A newly identified Jurassic bird may finally provide the missing piece, but not in the way researchers expected.

title: Ancient cave discovery changes what we know about relationship between Neanderthals and humans
description: The two closely related species coexisted as friends, sharing elements of their culture
